title: The personal-data request register of rwb-access has no table, no operation set, no statutory period, no state set and no link to the case hold in the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-016); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.27); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1, T6.1, T7, appendix T-A); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-UNI-11); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md (REQ-S8-007, NFR-043)
description: No source names a register table or an operation set for a PDPA access, correction or erasure request, the statutory period's value, day-count basis or owner, the state set of a request and the late flag, the record codes of a receipt and an outcome, the shape of the subject reference, or the link by which a recorded request reaches the case hold that R-UNI-11 requires. The ownership map names five tables for P4 and none of them is a request register.
evidence: RWB-E8-016 gives one screen and two rule-version endpoints (POST /admin/rule-versions and its approve), which are RWB-P4-E8007-APP and RWB-P4-E8011-APP now, and three data rows (decision_log_entry, rule_row, role); FSD P4 v3 A2.27 gives the intent, the metric, the three steps, VR-P4-027-1, VR-P4-027-2, BR-P4-027 and AC-P4-027-01 with AC-EXC-P4-027-01 and -02, and no operation and no field; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 lists delegation_limit, masking_rule, permission, role, role_conflict and the rule tables, and no request table; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and no personal-data operation; NFR-043 says 'Statutory period, Not set as a working service level, Open, DL26'; R-UNI-11 names the timer 'statutory period' and the state HELD_LEGAL, which is a case state of P3; the ownership map puts case and task with P3, document with P5 and decision_log_entry with P7.
proposed: Build the register as the local decision-record chain of DP-03 in rwb_access with a receipt entry and an outcome entry per request, four operations on /api/recovery/access/v1/personal-data/requests, the state set RECEIVED, ANSWERED and REFUSED with late as a derived flag, the statutory period as a parameter row of rwb-case read through DP-06 with its version label recorded as the rule version, and references only (subjectRef, caseRef) so that no personal data enters the register or the record; leave the case hold to rwb-case and raise the missing link as a dependency for D1.

title: The contract surface of the personal-data request register is not in the sources, and the statutory period has no value and no name
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml
description: The four paths, the four schema names and their field sets, the error set of each operation, the subject-reference shape, the request-type and channel sets, the parameter row names of the statutory period and of the page bounds, the late flag as a contract element, the record codes of a receipt and an outcome, and the declaration that the case hold and the document erasure are neither provided nor consumed are not in the sources.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.27.3.2 gives the field catalog of role and permission only and no request field; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 declares no personal-data operation, and its T3.2 lists LOV-ROLE-CLASS, LOV-SCOPE, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-ROUTE-SET, LOV-RULE-TABLE and LOV-VERSION-STATUS and no request-type or channel list; the API Specification v4 declares no /personal-data path; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives the P4 contract as authorise, me/permissions, doa-limits and masking-policies; DP-06 gives the parameters contract of rwb-case and names no row of this capability.
proposed: Fix the four paths under /api/recovery/access/v1/personal-data/requests, the four schemas with references and codes only, the error set 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with their message IDs and MSG-P4-004 as a warning field, the state set RECEIVED, ANSWERED and REFUSED with the late flag derived, and the consumed authorise and parameters operations with their owners; hold the period, the sets, the subject-reference shape and the page bounds as parameter rows and declare no number in the document.

title: Three sources disagree on who holds the right to work a data subject request
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-016 permission checks); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.27.3.3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T6.1, T6.2)
description: The legacy story gives the capability the Rules and parameters letters of another feature, C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, and names no capability area. The FSD role table names the Compliance and PDPA officer as primary and the security administrator as also using. TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-COMPLY R in Rules and parameters, RU in Reference data and R in Platform administration, and no A letter anywhere, while RW-SECADM holds CRUDA and RW-PLATADM CRUD in Platform administration. No source states which capability area holds a personal-data request or which letter the write needs.
evidence: RWB-E8-016 permission checks table: 'Rules and parameters | C | RW-COE' and 'Rules and parameters | A | RW-RISK'; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.3.3: 'Compliance and PDPA officer | Primary' and 'Security administrator | Also uses'; TSD P4 v3 T6.1: 'RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | R | RU | R' and 'RW-SECADM Security administrator | R | R | CRUDA'; TSD P4 v3 T6.2: 'each endpoint declares its capability area and right'; the two screens the legacy story names, SCR-47 Personal data and SCR-39 Rules and parameters, belong to different journeys (FSD P4 v3 screen list).
proposed: Read the capability area of a data subject request as PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION, the write as the U letter and the reads as the R letter, and grant RW-COMPLY the U letter in PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION at the matrix load of RWB-P4-E1037-APP so that the FSD primary role can do the work while the T6.1 columns stay unchanged for every other role; carry the legacy Rules and parameters letters of RW-COE and RW-RISK as not applicable to this capability.
